title: Aniimo Title Promotion Guide | Student To Trailblazer And Every Level Cap | Aniimo Guide
description: How title promotions and level caps work in Aniimo: the Student, Wayfarer and Trailblazer ladder with the level cap of every title, Elite Training objectives, the Dr Lewis promotion assessment, Report Cards and Talents, and what changes after level sixty. Checked against several guides in November 2026; some requirements differ between guides and patches change them, so check the Elite Training screen in your own game.

sections.heading: Intro
sections.script: Have you ever hit a level and suddenly your experience stopped mattering? In Aniimo that is not a bug. It is the level cap, and the only way past it is a title promotion. These promotions take you from Student, through Wayfarer, all the way up to Trailblazer, and every step raises how strong you and your Aniimo can get. In this video we go through the whole ladder, what each title unlocks, how the promotion assessment works, and what to do when you are stuck. A quick note. Guides disagree on some exact requirements, so check the Elite Training screen in your own game for the final word.

sections.heading: Why level caps exist
sections.script: Your character does not simply level up forever. Each title sets a ceiling, and guides say a promotion raises both your character level cap and your Aniimo level cap by the same amount. That is why a promotion feels like a big moment. The same upgrade that lets you grow also lets every Aniimo on your team grow. Guides also point out that research level is a separate system, and it does not raise your cap. So no matter how many entries you fill in your Aniilog, you still need the promotion. This is why many players feel stuck, and the answer is almost always the same. Do the training and take the test. Think of the cap as a gate that opens only when you prove you have practiced the game's systems, not just fought wild Aniimo for hours.

sections.heading: The Student titles
sections.script: The ladder starts with the Student titles. Guides list the caps like this. Student one gives you a cap of twenty five, Student two raises it to thirty five, and Student three raises it to forty. Two guides describe the second step as lifting both caps from twenty five to thirty five, and one example for the third step needs you to reach character level thirty five and finish four required quests from chapter two. These early promotions happen naturally if you follow the main story and the Elite Training chapters, so most players pass them without even planning for it.

sections.heading: The Wayfarer titles
sections.script: Next come the three Wayfarer titles. Wayfarer one raises the cap to forty five, Wayfarer two raises it to fifty, and Wayfarer three raises it to fifty five. Here the guides start to disagree on the exact character level you need before the test opens. One wiki lists lower numbers than another guide, and a main story quest is said to check for level fifty plus the Wayfarer three title. So treat the cap numbers as the ceiling you gain, not the exact level you must hit first. This is also the stage where the story gets harder, so make sure your team is strong before you push on.

sections.heading: The Trailblazer titles
sections.script: Now the top of the ladder. Trailblazer one raises your cap to sixty, Trailblazer two raises it to sixty five, and the Whisperwake Isles update added Trailblazer three, which lifts both your character and Aniimo caps to seventy. That update went live at the end of October. Guides also say that past level sixty, your Aniimo need an Ascension that uses an Evolution Item matching their main element. Trailblazer one is also the title that opens the weekly Holo-Battle Interlink boss mode, so this is where the endgame really begins.

sections.heading: How a promotion works step by step
sections.script: Every promotion follows the same pattern. First, open Elite Training from the main menu and look at your current chapter. Complete the required course objectives, and guides say that is usually four core objectives. Second, talk to Dr Lewis at the Outpost. He gives you the Promotion Assessment mission. Third, clear that mission. Fourth, go back to Dr Lewis and pass the final theory questionnaire, which is multiple choice. Many questions are common sense, such as choosing the answer that says all of the above, but read each one carefully anyway. Pass it, and your new title and higher caps arrive straight away.

sections.heading: Report Cards and Talents
sections.script: Promotions also give you something very useful. Two guides say you get Report Cards, which are the talent points you spend on the Talents screen. They unlock active and passive abilities for your Pathfinder, and you choose what to upgrade yourself, so think before you spend. Report Cards also come from other sources, including your Aniilog level, journey quests and the Elite Pathfinder Challenge. Promotions can also bring new character skills, a higher world level and extra challenge rewards. So even if you do not care about levels, a promotion is a free power boost that you should never skip for too long.

sections.heading: What to do while you are capped
sections.script: What should you do when you hit the cap and the promotion is not ready? First, stop wasting time grinding. Go to the Elite Training screen and read exactly what is missing. Often it is a single objective, like a quest, a catch, or a level for a specific Aniimo. Second, work on things that do not need levels, such as Homeland, breeding, collecting badges and your Aniilog. One guide says surplus character experience is stored while you wait, but that Aniimo experience is not, so do not rush to farm Aniimo experience before the test. Treat the cap as a signal to do something different. A short break from levelling is also a good time to claim your daily rewards, spend your Primegy, and check that your Homeland workers are busy, because all of that keeps progressing while you wait. Many players come back to the promotion refreshed and finish it in a single evening.

sections.heading: Common mistakes
sections.script: Here are the mistakes that waste the most time. First, reading a guide's level number as a rule. Different guides give different thresholds, and your Elite Training screen is the only truth. Second, forgetting to report a catch at the Research Console when the counter does not move. Third, grinding experience on the wrong Aniimo while you wait for the promotion. Fourth, ignoring your Report Cards and leaving talent points unspent. And finally, rushing the theory test without reading the questions. Fix those five and promotions become fast and almost painless. One more small tip. Take a screenshot of your Elite Training requirements before you log off, so you can plan your next session and know exactly what is left to do.

sections.heading: A simple promotion plan
sections.script: Here is a simple plan you can follow. Open Elite Training every time you reach your current cap. Finish the core objectives. Visit Dr Lewis at the Outpost, clear the assessment mission and pass the questionnaire. Spend your Report Cards on the talents that help your play style the most. Then raise your Aniimo to the new cap and repeat. If you do this every time, you will move from Student to Trailblazer without ever feeling stuck, and you will arrive at the endgame modes with a strong team and a full talent tree.

sections.heading: Over to you
sections.script: That is our guide to title promotions and level caps in Aniimo. Now tell us. Which title are you on right now, and which promotion gave you the most trouble? Was it a missing objective, a boss, or the theory test? Write it in the comments, because your answer might help another player break through their cap.
